When I was born, I had two parents who adored me. The little time I spent with them was incredible, though it wasn't much (2–3 days a week). For some reason, they were always visiting the city. I was 5 years old and didn't understand why. I used to stay with a beautiful lady. She had bright eyes, long black hair, and looked like someone in her 50s, but very well-preserved.

One day, I woke up at home and no one was there. Scared, being only a 6-year-old child, I started searching around. There was no one, so I went to look in the mountains where we used to go hiking. I got completely lost, and meanwhile, daybreak was coming. A whole day passed. Trying to find my way, I encountered an enormous, terrifying creature draped in a blue mantle. He was injured, with massive rocks capable of weighing tons lying on his left side, covering even his majestic wing and one of his eyes. He tried to push me away in every possible way, but I didn't understand him—I was just trying to help pull him out of that trap. With only seconds left of his final breath, the dragon absorbed part of my air genasi essence, which gave him enough strength to lift the rocks. He felt that there was something inside me, though he didn't quite understand what, and proceeded to help me find my parents as a token of gratitude.

After 1 year of intensive searching, Nyra gives up, but now, as a consolation, she has a grumpy yet loyal life companion. Despite his impaired flight, Kelvin (the dragon) makes fun of Nyra's lack of skills, since she only knows how to hunt (taught by her parents and refined by the dragon). Blue dragons are known for gathering gold in the mountains, but since Kelvin is debilitated and cannot do so, Nyra is forced to go to the city to sell whatever she catches from hunting.

On the day she turns 18, all the vendors who know her in the city gather together. In the middle of this celebration, an old woman with gray hair and wrinkled skin appears in a panic, catching the attention of Nyra, who goes over to talk to her. I take her to a corner, and she tells me to meet her at 11:59 PM in Moonlight Alley. Intrigued, Nyra shows up without telling Kelvin. When she arrives, Ghavel (the old woman) hands her a box. Inside the massive box are manuscripts, riddles, unrecognizable photographs, and a smaller box that won't open. I ask what all of that is, and she tells me that before my parents disappeared/died, they said that all their research was inside that large box, and if anything happened to them, she should go to their house in the city and hide the box with her (I had no idea they owned a house in the city). Inside the box was a photo that read "only you can decipher this," as if it were meant to find me—though Ghavel thought I had vanished along with them, until she searched my house in the mountains.

I return to Kelvin's company and tell him everything that happened. He calls me stupid and says this is a suicide mission: if whatever it was killed my parents, what would it do to me? We start arguing, so I grab the box and vanish into the mountains, trying to begin deciphering the riddles.

After spending the entire night thinking about it all, I realize that if I combine the loose pages, I can form an encrypted journal. I then return to my house in the city to learn more about this supposed treasure hunt. I spend a full week there until I manage to decipher a creature type: elementals. I research the subject and discover that 4 types exist (air, fire, water, and earth), with the air elemental hiding in the mountains. But what should I do with them? Why are they important?

After talking with Ghavel about all this, I finally realize that I need to destroy part of the soul of an elemental of each type. I start with the place I know best: the mountains, to try and capture part of the soul of the air elemental.

After 1 year of searching, and with Kelvin's help, I finally find it inside a dark cavern called the Cavern of Discovery. When I go in to face it, completely unaware of how to actually do it, I get an absolute beating and come close to dying—until Kelvin saves me with what little strength he has left, though he could never defeat it alone. That is when a strange force begins to take over my body. Energy starts flowing through me as the air elemental attacks, but Kelvin reveals an ability called Cold Breath that he had learned 100 years prior. With this mysterious force, I combat the incoming winds from the elemental until it freezes into a block of ice. As a final blow, I shoot an arrow into its center, and part of its soul drops in the form of a crystal. I pick up a long staff I find in the Cavern of Discovery and tie the soul crystal to the top of it.

Exhausted, Kelvin and I exit the cavern and have a deep conversation. He tells me that from now on we are even, and that I will have to complete this quest without him; I understand. I say goodbye for now and go the following day to speak with Ghavel, because something won't leave my mind: How was I able to control air?

She explains that both of my parents were "air genasi," a lineage among rangers, and they knew these powers would eventually awaken in me, but didn't want to tell me at such an early age. She asks what I intend to do now, considering I nearly died killing the very first elemental, and tells me I won't be able to do it alone.

This leads me to find a group of adventurers who will join this journey to help me find my parents—because I discovered that they might not be dead after all, only captured.
